description: Comprehensive coronary artery tree for cardiac education

vessels.name: Left Main Coronary Artery
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Supplies LAD and LCx regardless of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Critical structure - left main disease is surgical indication. Judkins Left or EBU catheter for engagement.

lesionSeverityHooks.mild: Minimal flow limitation, monitor with serial imaging
lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Catastrophic - usually fatal unless extensive collaterals present

vessels.name: Proximal Left Anterior Descending
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Proximal LAD lesions carry high risk. Supplies large territory including septum via septal perforators.

lesionSeverityHooks.severe: High-risk lesion, PCI or CABG depending on anatomy
lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Large anterior STEMI with significant LV dysfunction risk

vessels.name: Mid Left Anterior Descending
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Common site for PCI. Wire and stent delivery usually straightforward.

vessels.name: Distal Left Anterior Descending
vessels.dominanceRelevance: May wrap around apex in some patients
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Smaller vessel, CTO attempts may be challenging. Wraparound LAD supplies inferior apex.

lesionSeverityHooks.severe: PCI if large territory at risk

vessels.name: First Diagonal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Bifurcation lesions at LAD-D1 require special strategies. May need two-stent technique.

vessels.name: Second Diagonal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Smaller branch, PCI less commonly indicated unless large.

vessels.name: First Septal Perforator
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Important landmark for proximal LAD. Septal ablation target in HOCM.

vessels.name: Second Septal Perforator
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Mid-septal territory supply.

vessels.name: Ramus Intermedius
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Present as trifurcation variant of left main
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: When present, creates a trifurcation that complicates left main intervention.

lesionSeverityHooks.moderate: Assess territory size — can be as large as a diagonal

vessels.name: Proximal Left Circumflex
vessels.dominanceRelevance: In left-dominant systems, gives rise to PDA
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Engagement with JL or EBU catheter. LAO caudal view best for visualization.

lesionSeverityHooks.severe: PCI recommended especially in left-dominant systems
lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Lateral STEMI, more extensive if left-dominant

vessels.name: Distal Left Circumflex
vessels.dominanceRelevance: In left-dominant: gives rise to PDA and posterolateral branches
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: May be small in right-dominant systems. Important in left-dominant.

vessels.name: First Obtuse Marginal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Present in all dominance patterns
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Common PCI target. Bifurcation with LCx may require special technique.

vessels.name: Second Obtuse Marginal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Present in all dominance patterns
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Smaller branch, PCI less common.

vessels.name: Third Obtuse Marginal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Not always present
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Small branch, rarely target for PCI.

vessels.name: Proximal Right Coronary Artery
vessels.dominanceRelevance: In right-dominant systems (~85%), supplies PDA and AV node
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: JR4 or AR catheter for engagement. RAO view for proximal visualization.

lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Inferior STEMI with potential RV involvement and AV block

vessels.name: Mid Right Coronary Artery
vessels.dominanceRelevance: In right-dominant systems, critical conduit to PDA
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Often tortuous segment. Common site for CTO.

vessels.name: Distal Right Coronary Artery
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Bifurcates into PDA and posterolateral branches in right-dominant
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Crux of the heart — critical bifurcation point.

lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Inferior MI with AV nodal ischemia

vessels.name: Conus Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance, may arise from aorta directly
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Collateral pathway to LAD territory via Vieussens ring.

vessels.name: SA Nodal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: From RCA in 55%, from LCx in 45%
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Rarely target for PCI. Important in understanding post-MI sinus node dysfunction.

lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Sinus node ischemia, bradycardia, sick sinus

vessels.name: Acute Marginal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Independent of dominance
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Important for RV territory assessment.

lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: RV infarction contributing to hemodynamic instability

vessels.name: Posterior Descending Artery
vessels.dominanceRelevance: From RCA in right-dominant (85%), from LCx in left-dominant (8%), both in codominant (7%)
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Determines coronary dominance. Supplies AV node branch in most patients.

lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Inferior septal infarction, AV block risk

vessels.name: Posterolateral Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: Present in right-dominant systems
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Part of dominant RCA territory.

lesionSeverityHooks.severe: Part of overall RCA territory assessment

vessels.name: AV Nodal Branch
vessels.dominanceRelevance: From dominant artery — RCA in right-dominant, LCx in left-dominant
vessels.catheterizationRelevance: Not a PCI target. Important in understanding conduction disturbances in MI.

lesionSeverityHooks.occlusion: Complete heart block in inferior MI
